label: GPT-6.1 Terra
output:
The Winter School on Elliptic Curves and Modular Forms wrapped up on Saturday, and on behalf of the organising team, I want to thank everyone who made it possible.

From 5–7 November, we had 41 MSc and early PhD participants from 9 states at the Department of Mathematics, Sahyadri Institute of Science, Pune. We received 112 applications and selected participants based on a statement and one reference. It was encouraging to see so much interest in spending three days working through mathematics together.

Thank you to our speakers: Dr. Nilesh Dharmadhikari (Hyderabad) for Mordell–Weil, Dr. Sunanda Iyer (Chennai) for modular forms, and Dr. Tomasz Wierzbicki, who joined us online from Kraków for computations in Sage. We are grateful to our faculty mentor, Prof. Anuradha Venkatesan, for her guidance throughout.

One moment I will remember: an MSc student from Silchar spotted an error in a worked example in Sunanda ma’am’s notes. She corrected it live and thanked him. That kind of exchange was exactly what we hoped the school would make room for.

On the second afternoon, the power went out for nearly two hours and laptops died. We moved the problem session to the canteen with two rolling whiteboards. It turned out to be the best session of the three days.

Thank you to the six PhD students who volunteered as teaching assistants and ran the problem sessions. The format worked well, and we hope to keep it. Thank you also to Mr. Prakash Salunke, who sorted out hostel rooms at 11 pm when a booking went wrong, and to all the participants for bringing their questions and energy.

The institute’s student initiative grant of Rs 2.4 lakh covered hostel stays and travel for 18 outstation students. We are grateful for that support. It made it possible for students from outside Pune to take part.

I enjoyed organising this with Ketaki Joglekar and Faizan Mirza. Small schools like this can matter more than big conferences for MSc students: there is time to ask questions, work through problems and learn from one another.

We plan to share the slides and problem sheets on the department website within two weeks. We hope to run a second edition in late 2027, subject to grant funding.
